campbell.title: Campbell City Council — November 2, 2026
campbell.summary: The source for the November 2, 2026, Campbell City Council meeting is a video transcript, so this describes what the transcript shows was before the Council. The agenda centered on a proposal to replace the Campbell Technology Park office campus with a 290-home housing development (27 single-family homes and 263 townhome-style condos, 20% affordable). It also included a contract for police recruitment advertising and the consent calendar, with neighborhood speakers raising concerns about housing in single-family areas during open public comment.
keyTopics: Campbell Technology Park redevelopment: certify the environmental report, approve a planned development permit and vesting tentative subdivision map for 290 homes (27 detached homes, 263 townhome-style condos), remove 116 trees, and increase fence/wall height to 8 ft along Highway 17. Staff described it as a 'builder's remedy' project, meaning the city has limited ability to deny or reduce it under state housing law.

Traffic and safety for the housing project: staff reported no significant unavoidable impacts, with required pedestrian crosswalk upgrades near Campbell Technology Parkway and McGlincy Lane. Council members raised concerns about congestion, pedestrian/bike access, and the redwood trees along the Paseo de Palomas boundary.

Police recruitment contract: a one-year agreement with All Star Talent to run online recruiting and marketing for the police department, skipping the normal bidding process, funded from $175,000 in the 2026-27 budget.

Open public comment: residents of the White Oaks Manor neighborhood spoke about demolition of single-family homes for townhome projects and a proposed demolition control ordinance, and another speaker proposed fundraising for pedestrian safety measures.

Council announcements and consent calendar: reminders about the November 3 election and ballot deadlines, open board and commission vacancies, Veterans Day events, and consent calendar items 7.1 to 7.6.

saratoga.title: Saratoga City Council — November 4, 2026
saratoga.summary: The agenda for the Saratoga City Council's November 4, 2026, meeting listed routine business items, a public hearing on a proposed temporary pause on certain detention-related facilities, and a proposed contract for an outside review of how the city is organized. Residents were also given time to speak on topics not on the agenda.
keyTopics: Public hearing on an urgent, temporary moratorium on establishing or operating detention or custodial detention facilities and custodial processing facilities while the city studies appropriate zoning and land use rules; the agenda proposes finding it exempt from CEQA under Guidelines section 15061(b)(3)
Proposed agreement with Bell Burnette & Atwater (BB&A) for an organizational assessment, at a cost of no more than $165,000 for fiscal year 2026-27

2026 Annual Code Update on the consent calendar, an ordinance amending many city code sections, including accessory dwelling units, urban lot splits, tree regulations, design review, density bonus and inclusionary housing rules, and housing on faith and higher education lands
Proposed revised Citywide Records Retention Schedule, listed on the consent calendar for adoption by resolution
Routine consent items: approving October 21 meeting minutes, accepting the October 22 accounts payable check registers, and accepting the Treasurer's Report for the month ended September 30, 2026

los-altos.title: Los Altos City Council — October 27, 2026
los-altos.summary: The agenda for the October 27, 2026, Los Altos City Council meeting listed routine business such as purchasing city vehicles and awarding contracts for a park expansion and a Police Department backup generator. It also listed a proposed salary amendment for the City Manager, an extension of a temporary moratorium on certain detention and custodial facilities, and a presentation from Cal Water on water conservation.
keyTopics: The agenda listed a contract with Lignum Mellis of San Francisco for the Building B Park Expansion Project, not to exceed $166,225, with up to 10% in additional construction contingency.
The agenda listed a $417,400 contract with ELECCO of Milpitas to replace the Police Department's backup generator, with a construction contingency of up to 15%.

The agenda listed an amendment to the City Manager's employment agreement setting an annual base salary of $375,000 effective July 5, 2026, plus an annual CPI/general salary adjustment provision starting July 2027.
The agenda listed an interim urgency ordinance extending Ordinance No. 2026-548, a temporary moratorium related to detention or custodial facilities and custodial processing facilities.

The agenda listed a Cal Water presentation on water conservation measures, a resolution on a Transit Signal Priority Policy on behalf of VTA, and a resolution to buy three replacement maintenance vehicles and one piece of equipment.

los-gatos.title: Los Gatos Town Council — November 2, 2026
los-gatos.summary: The agenda for the Los Gatos Town Council's November 2, 2026, meeting listed routine business items, including approval of minutes from the October 20 meetings and ratification of the Town's bills and payroll. It also listed several contract-related items and a proposed change to the salary schedule for the Town Employees Association.
keyTopics: Minutes from the October 20, 2026, regular and closed session Town Council meetings were listed for approval.
The agenda listed approval and ratification of the accounts payable check registers and the payroll report.
Two items asked the Council to authorize the Town Manager to sign agreements for professional services.
The Council was asked to consider authorizing the Town Manager to sign a second amendment to an existing agreement.
The agenda listed an amendment to the Town Employees Association (TEA) salary schedule.

san-jose.title: San José City Council — November 10, 2026
san-jose.summary: The agenda for the November 10, 2026, San José City Council meeting listed a mix of housing, traffic, emergency preparedness, and historic preservation items. Items for consideration included agreements for a new family center in Blossom Valley, an amended development agreement with Apple, and an update on El Niño flood preparedness that includes a proclamation of a local emergency.
keyTopics: Agreements with Catholic Charities of Santa Clara County and the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development for developing the Blossom Valley Family Center
Funding agreement with the Santa Clara Valley Transportation Authority for deploying an adaptive traffic control system on San José arterial streets
El Niño update, flood preparedness, and a proclamation of a local emergency

Historic landmark designations and Mills Act contracts for properties including 231 Jackson Street (Kogura Company Building), 605 North 6th Street (Kow Kee Sixplex), 495-497 North 13th Street and 580-584 East Empire Street, and Hotel De Anza at 233 West Santa Clara Street
First amendment to the amended and restated development agreement with Apple Inc. for sites on both sides of Orchard Parkway near Atmel Way and Component Drive

mountain-view.title: Mountain View City Council — November 10, 2026
mountain-view.summary: The agenda for the Mountain View City Council's November 10, 2026, regular session (6:30 p.m.) listed proclamations, a commendation for City Manager Kimbra McCarthy, and items on El Niño storm preparation, park and building projects, water and turf rules, and climate planning. It also listed a proposed appointment of a new City Attorney.
keyTopics: El Niño preparation: an update and an emergency declaration and funding appropriation for the 2026-27 El Niño climate pattern were listed.
Code amendments restricting use of drinking-quality (potable) water to irrigate nonfunctional turfgrass, along with an update to the recycled water service area.
Climate items: the 2024 Community Greenhouse Gas Emissions Inventory and the Climate Forward Plan.

Parks and facilities: an application for state park funding for Thompson Mini Park, design agreements for the Rengstorff House restoration and the Shoreline Boathouse expansion, Adobe Building patio tile replacement, and proposed changes to Chapter 38 of the City Code on use of city parks and facilities.
Appointment of Justin Mates as City Attorney and authorization of an employment agreement, plus the Rowhouse Gatekeeper Project at 924-940 San Rafael Avenue.

sunnyvale.title: Sunnyvale City Council — November 10, 2026
sunnyvale.summary: The agenda listed a closed-session special meeting at 6 p.m., followed by the regular 7 p.m. Council meeting. Items on the agenda included a water-facility equipment contract, retiree and employee health contribution rates, updates to city policies, new rules for splitting lots and building additional homes under state law, and changes to the city's affordable housing in-lieu fees.
keyTopics: The agenda listed a second amendment to the Clean Water Facility instrumentation contract with Endress+Hauser Inc., raising the not-to-exceed amount to $445,000 and extending it through October 18, 2027.

The agenda listed an ordinance to repeal and re-adopt Sunnyvale's urban lot split and dual urban opportunity housing rules to match state SB 9 changes, along with related changes to reduced and deferred development impact fees.

The agenda listed changes to the Council Policy Manual, including adding parental leave for Councilmembers and deleting six outdated policies (water metering for condominiums, polystyrene food products, energy, powered equipment, human services, environmental procurement).
The agenda listed proposed changes to the Below Market Rate in-lieu fees, including converting the ownership fee to a square-footage basis and periodic reviews of the inclusionary housing policy.
The agenda included a request to continue the residential off-street parking requirements ordinance to December 1, 2026.

cupertino.title: Cupertino City Council — November 2, 2026
cupertino.summary: The agenda for the November 2, 2026, Cupertino City Council meeting listed presentations from three sister cities (Toyokawa, Hsinchu, and Bhubaneswar), a set of routine consent calendar items, and a study session on updating the city's emergency plan. Among the consent items were a roughly $11.8 million budget change to buy a property on Finch Avenue and a grant and design contract for the McClellan Road Bridge. No public hearings were listed.
keyTopics: Sister city presentations were listed from Toyokawa and Hsinchu on recent student exchanges, and from Bhubaneswar on recent activities.
A budget modification was listed to add $11,825,000 to the Parkland Dedication Fund to purchase the Finch Property at 10480 Finch Avenue.

A resolution was listed for the McClellan Road Bridge Project: accepting $850,000 in Caltrans-administered grant funds and awarding a design services agreement to Biggs Cardosa Associates, Inc. for up to $1,278,700.
A study session was listed on proposed updates to the city's 2019 Emergency Operations Plan.

Housing and community funding items were listed: a $114,546 increase and extension through December 31, 2027, for the Vista Village CDBG agreement, and renewal of the city's participation in the Santa Clara County Permanent Local Housing Allocation Consortium.

santa-clara.title: Santa Clara City Council and Authorities Concurrent — November 10, 2026
santa-clara.summary: The agenda for the November 10, 2026, Santa Clara City Council and Stadium Authority meeting listed a closed session on legal matters at 5:00 PM, followed by a 7:00 PM joint public meeting. Items before the Council included a proposed 44-townhouse development, a new sustainability manager position, updated city salary plans, and several contracts for Levi's Stadium, tree care, and Silicon Valley Power. The meeting was set up for in-person attendance and for participation by Zoom, phone, eComment, or email.
keyTopics: Public hearing on the Agrihood Project at 1816 Worthington Circle: rezoning from Planned Development to Medium Density Residential and a subdivision map to allow 44 townhouse units
Request to add a 1.0 full-time Division Manager position in the City Manager's Office of Economic Development and Sustainability to serve as the Sustainability Manager
Resolutions to adopt updated classified, unclassified, and as-needed salary plans, including negotiated cost-of-living wage adjustments

Levi's Stadium items: as-needed architectural and engineering agreements with HKS Architects, Hellmuth, Obata & Kassabaum, and Populous Design Build (up to $7.5 million each, $15 million total spending cap), a $146,315.02 asphalt replacement contract with Graham Contractors, and a security improvements budget amendment
Vice Mayor Gonzalez's request to place a future agenda item on adopting an urgency ordinance for a temporary moratorium on detention centers

milpitas.title: Milpitas City Council — October 20, 2026
milpitas.summary: The agenda for the October 20, 2026, Milpitas City Council meeting listed routine business such as meeting calendars and minutes, along with a proposed contract change for a new park design, a presentation on mosquito control, and a proposal to rename two city sites and name a new community garden. It also listed the annual review of the city's advisory commissions and their plans for the coming year.
keyTopics: The agenda listed an amendment to the design contract with Callander Associates Landscape Architecture for the Metro Tango Subdistrict Park, for an amount not to exceed $130,000.

A resolution on the agenda would rename the Cesar Chavez Community Garden to "Milpitas Community Garden," rename Cesar Chavez Plaza to "Milpitas Civic Center Plaza," and name the garden in Delano Manongs Park the "Larry Itliong Community Garden."
The Santa Clara County Mosquito and Vector Control District was listed to give a presentation to the Council.

The Council was scheduled to consider accepting the FY2025-26 annual report from city commissions and approving FY2026-27 work plans for eight commissions, including the Arts Commission, Economic Development and Trade Commission, and Library and Education Advisory Commission.
Routine items listed included the October and November 2026 meeting calendar, the October 6, 2026, meeting minutes, and lists of upcoming and Councilmember-requested agenda items.

palo-alto.title: Palo Alto City Council — October 26, 2026
palo-alto.summary: The agenda for the October 26, 2026, Palo Alto City Council meeting listed a mix of routine appointments and consent items alongside several policy items, including winter storm preparedness, stream corridor protections, a pause on new detention facilities, and a proposed expansion of human services funding. The agenda also listed a closed-session discussion about the price and payment terms for a property at 1900 Embarcadero Road.
keyTopics: The agenda listed a review of the city's 2026-2027 winter storm preparedness activities, with a staff presentation and public comment.
The agenda listed a proposed expansion of the Human Services Resource Allocation Process (HSRAP) for FY 2028-2029, with $428,000 in additional annual funding.
The agenda listed a temporary ordinance to impose a moratorium on new or expanded detention and custodial facilities within Palo Alto city limits, with public comment.
The agenda listed an ordinance amending the Stream Corridor Protection section of the municipal code (18.40.140), with a supplemental report added, a staff presentation, and public comment.

The agenda listed a closed-session conference with real property negotiators about the price and payment terms for 1900 Embarcadero Road, with BioScience Property Investments named as the negotiating party.
